traveler: Marta María Ezcurra Real de Azúa
title: El Azote de Dios: from the Hijas de María to the Dissolution of the Fundación Eva Perón
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta, the vault the surname opens
stops.date_confidence: attested for Encarnación Ezcurra's death and burial. Pin inherited byte-identical from juan_manuel_de_rosas.journey.json, 'La Recoleta, the bones brought home'. Marta Ezcurra is placed in this vault by no source; the stop marks the lineage, not a grave.
stops.campa: Sixty-two years before Marta is born, Encarnación Ezcurra is laid in the family vault at the Recoleta. She was the wife of Juan Manuel de Rosas and the sharper operator of the pair, builder of the federalist street league while her husband held the countryside. Her brother José María Ezcurra is Marta's great-great-grandfather. In 1989 Rosas himself comes home to lie a short walk from her. The surname Marta carries is this one; whether her own bones ever reach this ground, no source consulted says.
suggested_refs: The Ezcurra family vault, Cementerio de la Recoleta, Buenos Aires
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Pedro Ezcurra' (José María Ezcurra as cuñado of Rosas)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth in a contested year
stops.date_confidence: contested and unresolved. Las Balas del Campanario (2020) gives 2 May 1900; es.wikipedia's Hospital Escuela Eva Perón gives 'Marta María Ezcurra (1901-¿?)', footnoted to her electoral-roll entry, CUIT 27-00227996-2. Neither is a birth registry. 1900-05-02 is carried here for ordering only. Pin is the canonical central Buenos Aires coordinate: no address for the birth is given by any source.
stops.campa: A daughter is born in Buenos Aires to Pedro Dionisio Ezcurra, engineer, and Marta Real de Azúa Muñoz, married six years before. They name her Marta María. She is the fourth of twelve. The house is old porteño Catholic money with a ministry attached: her father will sit in the cabinet of José Figueroa Alcorta within seven years. No parish register for the birth has been found, and the two sources that give a year do not agree on it. She enters the record already as a date under dispute, and she will leave it the same way.
suggested_refs: Argentine electoral-roll entry for Marta María Ezcurra, CUIT 27-00227996-2, cited in es.wikipedia's Hospital Escuela Eva Perón
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11: Marta Ezcurra, encargada de destruir la obra social peronista', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the father in the cabinet
stops.date_confidence: attested (es.wikipedia, 'Pedro Ezcurra'): Minister of Agriculture 4 November 1907 to 12 October 1910; born 9 October 1860, died 8 October 1913. No ministry address given; canonical central Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: Pedro Dionisio Ezcurra takes the Ministry of Agriculture under President José Figueroa Alcorta and holds it just short of three years. His daughter is seven. He dies on the eighth of October 1913, one day short of fifty-three, and she is thirteen or twelve depending on which birth year is right. The one popular account of her life garbles his name, calling him Pedro Tomás Dionisio de Ezcurra Pardo, which belongs to his own father. Even her father reaches the record through a mistake.
suggested_refs: Ministerio de Agricultura de la Nación under Figueroa Alcorta, 1907-1910
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Almagro, the Colegio del Sagrado Corazón
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Testa 2017: 'en 1915... recién egresada del Colegio Sagrado Corazón de Almagro'); month and day unknown and defaulted to 01-01. Pin is the Almagro neighbourhood centroid, declared as a placeholder: the school itself returns no result in any gazetteer consulted.
stops.campa: She leaves the Colegio del Sagrado Corazón in Almagro at fifteen, and the only scholar who has read the Catholic Action archive puts her there on the strength of one phrase: recién egresada. The convent school of the Sacred Heart in a middle-class parish teaches piety, French, and the management of a household. No class list survives from her year, and no photograph of it has been found. The building is in no gazetteer consulted, so the pin below stands for the neighbourhood and not for the school.
suggested_refs: Colegio del Sagrado Corazón, Almagro, Buenos Aires
sources: Daniela Testa, 'La lucha contra la poliomielitis y la figura de Marta Ezcurra. ¿Huellas del catolicismo social?', X JIDEEP, UNLP, 2017 (SEDICI 10915/64267)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Congregación Hijas de María
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Testa 2017); month, day and venue unknown. Pin is the canonical central Buenos Aires placeholder shared with alberto_gerchunoff and juan_manuel_de_rosas: no address for the sodality was found.
stops.campa: The same year she leaves school she enters the Congregación Hijas de María, and begins attending the apostolic and social formation meetings the Hermanas de la Asunción hold for young women of her class. A sodality is not a career. For most of the girls in the room it is a devotional habit that will survive marriage and change nothing else. Ezcurra treats it as an apprenticeship. Ten years of it stand between the schoolgirl and the woman who will sit on a Consejo Superior, and forty between her and a ministry.
suggested_refs: Congregación Hijas de María, Buenos Aires; formation meetings of the Hermanas de la Asunción

stops.name: Buenos Aires, El Centavo and the sewing workshops
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Testa 2017: joins El Centavo in 1925, later sitting on its Consejo Superior); month, day and premises unknown. Canonical central Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: At twenty-five she joins El Centavo, an association that assists needy women through food distribution and sewing workshops, and rises in time to its Consejo Superior. This is charity in the older Argentine manner: ladies of the parish, private subscription, the poor received rather than enfranchised. The Sociedad de Beneficencia model has run the country's welfare for a century and nobody in this room expects it to end. Twenty-three years later Eva Perón will say that where there is a need there is a right.
suggested_refs: El Centavo, Buenos Aires; the Sociedad de Beneficencia model of Argentine welfare before 1943

stops.name: Avenida Corrientes 1723, the Escuela de Servicio Social
stops.date_confidence: years attested (Testa 2017: 'En el año 1930 había ingresado a la recientemente fundada Escuela de Servicio Social del Museo Social Argentino, donde obtuvo el título de asistente social, en 1933'); months and days unknown. Coordinate corrected to the Museo Social Argentino at Av. Corrientes 1723; the research pool's pin was some 600 m off.
stops.campa: She enrols in the newly founded Escuela de Servicio Social del Museo Social Argentino, on Corrientes, and in 1933 takes the título de asistente social. She is among the first cohort of professionally certified social workers in Argentina. The popular accounts call the place the Universidad del Museo Social Argentino, which will not exist under that name until 1956; the anachronism is twenty-six years wide and travels intact through every retelling. What she acquires here is a technique, and a licence to apply it.
suggested_refs: Escuela de Servicio Social del Museo Social Argentino, Av. Corrientes 1723, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Primer Congreso Superior de las Jóvenes
stops.date_confidence: year attested, office contradicted and not resolved. Testa 2017: 'En 1931 fue nombrada presidenta del Primer Congreso Superior de las Jóvenes de la Acción Católica por el arzobispo Santiago Copello'. Four Spanish Wikipedia articles, all descending from Sandra Russo's Página/12 column of 17 September 2016, instead call her founder of the ACA youth branch. Month, day and venue unknown.
stops.campa: Archbishop Santiago Copello names her president of the First Superior Congress of the Young Women of Catholic Action. She is thirty-one. Acción Católica is the lay arm of the Argentine Church under episcopal direction, and its young women's wing is the seedbed from which a generation of Catholic activists will come. The popular version of her life says she founded the branch outright; the archive says she presided over its first congress. Both versions agree on one thing: from this year she speaks for it.
suggested_refs: Acción Católica Argentina, Junta Central; the Primer Congreso Superior de las Jóvenes, 1931
sources: Sandra Russo, 'Un lugar seguro', Página/12, 17 September 2016 (cited at second hand)

stops.name: Vatican City, the audience with Pius XI
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Testa 2017: travels to Europe in 1932 with a private audience with Pius XI 'en representación de la flamante Asociación de Jóvenes de la Acción Católica'); month and day unknown. Pin is the corpus-standard Vatican coordinate, inherited byte-identical.
stops.campa: She crosses to Europe and is received in private audience by Pius XI, representing the new Association of Young Women of Catholic Action. Pius XI is the pope of Quadragesimo anno, published the year before, and the pope who defines Catholic Action as the participation of the laity in the apostolate of the hierarchy. She comes home with the doctrine and with a papal hearing behind her name. Five years later she writes the manual that teaches it to Argentine girls, and it is reprinted.
suggested_refs: Quadragesimo anno (1931) and the Pian definition of Catholic Action

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Primeras Nociones de Doctrina Social Católica
stops.date_confidence: year attested (Testa 2017, fn. 5): manual issued by the Junta Central de la Acción Católica Argentina in 1937, second edition 1939. Month, day and place of printing unknown. Canonical central Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: The Junta Central de la Acción Católica Argentina issues her Primeras Nociones de Doctrina Social Católica as a manual, with a prologue by the economist Francisco Valsecchi. A second edition follows in 1939, the Junta explaining it by the favourable reception given to the little work. She also publishes lessons in Christian Sociology in the Catholic supplement Ideales. The title the internet gives her, Manual de Doctrina Social de la Iglesia, is one she never wrote; it survives because nobody checked.
stops.quote: Es que Marta Ezcurra ha dedicado desde la primera hora a la acción económico-social toda su inteligencia y entusiasmo.
stops.quote_source: Francisco Valsecchi, prologue to Primeras Nociones de Doctrina Social Católica (Junta Central de la Acción Católica Argentina, 1937), quoted in Testa 2017
suggested_refs: Marta Ezcurra, Primeras Nociones de Doctrina Social Católica, Junta Central de la ACA, 1937; 2nd ed. 1939
The Catholic supplement Ideales, lecciones de Sociología Cristiana
sources: Daniela Testa, X JIDEEP, UNLP, 2017 (SEDICI 10915/64267), incl. fn. 5

stops.name: Buenos Aires, la Asociación para la Lucha contra la Parálisis Infantil
stops.date_confidence: attested (Efemérides de Salta; corroborated by the SEDICI record of Testa 2017). The association's headquarters address was not located, so the canonical central Buenos Aires pin is used.
stops.campa: ALPI is founded in Buenos Aires on the seventeenth of December, a women's association for the fight against infantile paralysis, assisting poor children struck by polio. Argentina has no vaccine and no cure: what it has is rehabilitation, braces, and the iron lung. The founders are ladies; the staff are doctors. Ezcurra is among the founding group and will hold its highest office within a year. It is the first thing in her life that is neither a sodality nor a school, and it puts her hands on hospital machinery.
suggested_refs: Asociación para la Lucha contra la Parálisis Infantil (ALPI), founded 17 December 1943

stops.name: Buenos Aires, presidenta y vicepresidenta, alternadamente
stops.date_confidence: span attested, not the day: Testa 2017, 'Marta Ezcurra ocupó los cargos de presidenta y vicepresidenta alternadamente durante los primeros seis ejercicios (1944-1950)'. The research pool's 'president from 1943' was wrong on both the date and the shape of the office.
stops.campa: For six exercises she alternates between the presidency and the vice-presidency of ALPI. The historian who reads the association's own records describes what she builds there as an alliance of doctors and ladies held together by a scaffolding of Christian ideas. The formula is exact: the medicine is real, the money is private, the authority is Catholic, and the children are poor. This is the last decade in which such an arrangement runs Argentine welfare without a competitor. The competitor is already being built.
stops.quote: galenos y señoras constituyeron una alianza médico-social sostenida en un andamiaje de ideas cristianas
stops.quote_source: Daniela Testa, 'La lucha contra la poliomielitis y la figura de Marta Ezcurra', X JIDEEP, UNLP, 2017
suggested_refs: ALPI institutional records, exercises 1944-1950

stops.name: Salta, the branch opened four years after her last term
stops.date_confidence: attested (El Tribuno, 'Alpi festejará sus 60 años de vida en Salta', 2014; Salta efemérides). Pin is Salta city centre: the filial's address was not located. The research pool's clause tying the opening to Ezcurra's presidency is struck, her last term having ended in 1950.
stops.campa: ALPI opens a branch in Salta on the twelfth of June, with María Antonieta Day as its first president. The association Ezcurra helped found is now national. She is not running it: her last term ended four years earlier, and the popular account that credits her with the Salta opening credits her with something she was not in office for. The correction matters here more than elsewhere, because almost everything else written about her is written to make her larger.
suggested_refs: ALPI filial Salta, opened 12 June 1954, first president María Antonieta Day
sources: El Tribuno (Salta), 'Alpi festejará sus 60 años de vida en Salta', 2014

stops.name: Carlos Calvo 102, el Hogar de Tránsito N.º 1
stops.date_confidence: attested (es.wikipedia, 'Fundación Eva Perón'): the Foundation's first public act. Coordinate geocoded from the street address in San Telmo; the research pool's pin was some 750 m off. No source places Ezcurra here at any date, and no source says this specific building was occupied in 1955.
stops.campa: Eva Perón's first public act as a founder is the opening of a transit home at Carlos Calvo 102, in San Telmo: beds for women and children arriving in the capital with nowhere to go. There is no subscription list, no committee of ladies, no parish. There is a state, and a woman who says the poor are owed this. Seven years and six months later a different woman will hold the paper authorising the intervention of every institute the Foundation runs, and this address will be one line on it.
suggested_refs: Hogar de Tránsito N.º 1, Carlos Calvo 102, Buenos Aires, inaugurated 3 April 1948

stops.name: Buenos Aires, la Fundación Eva Perón
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin inherited byte-identical from eva_peron.journey.json, 'Fundación Eva Perón: donde hay una necesidad hay un derecho'. Legal personality granted 8 July 1948, with seat at Avenida Paseo Colón 850.
stops.campa: The Fundación Eva Perón is constituted on the nineteenth of June and receives legal personality on the eighth of July, with its seat at Avenida Paseo Colón 850. Eva Perón puts it in one sentence: donde hay una necesidad hay un derecho. Where there is a need there is a right, not a favour and not a donation. Everything Marta Ezcurra has spent thirty years building, the sodality, the workshops, the subscription, the alliance of doctors and ladies, is by that sentence made into the old regime.
suggested_refs: Fundación Eva Perón, personería jurídica 8 July 1948, seat at Av. Paseo Colón 850

stops.name: Echeverría 955, la Ciudad Infantil
stops.date_confidence: attested for the institution and its entrance address, Echeverría 955, Belgrano. Coordinate geocoded from that address. Flagged: eva_peron.journey.json pins the Ciudad Infantil at -34.627, -58.438, roughly 8 km south, in a different half of the city. Contradiction inside the corpus, recorded and not resolved.
stops.campa: The Ciudad Infantil Amanda Allen opens in Belgrano with its entrance on Echeverría: a small republic for children, with its own bank, its own municipality, its own shops, staffed to teach citizenship by rehearsing it. Attached to it is a Clínica de Recuperación with beds for the sick. Six years later a delegation will arrive at this gate, burn what is inside, and justify it by saying the care given to the minors here was sumptuous and unfit for the sobriety a republic owes its children.
suggested_refs: Ciudad Infantil Amanda Allen, Echeverría 955, Belgrano; today the Instituto de Rehabilitación Psicofísica

stops.name: Burzaco, the first home for the old
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim (es.wikipedia, 'Fundación Eva Perón': 'El 17 de octubre de 1949 se inauguró el primero de ellos en Burzaco y, hasta 1950, se abrieron otros cuatro'). Coordinate corrected to the Burzaco town centroid; the research pool's pin lay some 1.5 km to the south. No source places Ezcurra here.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of October, the Peronist national holiday, the first of the Foundation's homes for the aged opens at Burzaco in the southern suburbs. Four more follow by 1950. The date is not incidental: the anniversary of the crowd that filled the Plaza de Mayo in 1945 is the day the regime chooses for opening old people's homes. Six years later the homes are intervened along with everything else, and no source consulted places Marta Ezcurra at Burzaco or names who went.
suggested_refs: Hogar para Ancianos, Burzaco, Buenos Aires province, inaugurated 17 October 1949

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 869, el Hogar de la Empleada
stops.date_confidence: attested for the opening and the building's dimensions. Coordinate geocoded from the Monserrat address, some 320 m from the research pool's pin. Occupation of this specific building in 1955 is inference and is tagged [R]: the sources say only 'cada uno de los institutos'.
stops.campa: The Hogar de la Empleada General San Martín opens on Avenida de Mayo: eleven floors, nine of them dormitories, five hundred beds for working women earning under five hundred pesos a month. A single woman with a wage and no family in the capital can sleep in the centre of Buenos Aires for almost nothing. It is the most literal possible answer to what a working woman needs. No source says which day in 1955 it was taken, only that every institute was.
suggested_refs: Hogar de la Empleada General San Martín, Av. de Mayo 869, inaugurated 30 December 1949

stops.name: El Buen Pastor, San Telmo, the other Catholic institution
stops.date_confidence: attested for Victoria Ocampo's imprisonment; pin inherited byte-identical from victoria_ocampo.journey.json, 'Buenos Aires, El Buen Pastor, twenty-six days among the condemned'. Ezcurra is placed here by no source; the stop marks the institutional world she belongs to.
stops.campa: A women's penitentiary in San Telmo, El Buen Pastor has been run since 1890 by the Catholic Congregación del Buen Pastor for the correction of women. It is the far end of the tradition Ezcurra works in her whole career: Catholic sisters given legal custody of women and children the state has decided it cannot manage itself, workshops and cells built on the same premise. Ezcurra's own institutions sit at the gentler end of that continuum. In two years the direction of custody reverses, and it is Ezcurra doing the taking.
suggested_refs: El Buen Pastor women's penitentiary, San Telmo, run by the Congregación del Buen Pastor from 1890

stops.name: Córdoba city centre, the artillery school rises (site unlocated)
stops.date_confidence: attested to the hour (es.wikipedia, 'Comandos civiles': 'El 16 de septiembre de 1955 a las 00:00 horas el general Eduardo Lonardi sublevó la Escuela de Artillería de Córdoba, dando inicio al golpe'). Pin is Córdoba city centre, declared as a placeholder: the Escuela de Artillería returns no OSM or Nominatim result.
stops.campa: At midnight General Eduardo Lonardi raises the artillery school at Córdoba and the Revolución Libertadora begins against Perón. Nine days of uprising follow before Perón leaves power on the twentieth; Lonardi is sworn in as provisional president on the twenty-third, and Aramburu displaces him in turn on the thirteenth of November. None of it happens within reach of Marta Ezcurra's desk in Buenos Aires, yet within hours of Lonardi's oath the order to intervene the Fundación Eva Perón is already moving toward her.
suggested_refs: Escuela de Artillería, Córdoba, seized at 00:00 on 16 September 1955

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Lonardi sworn in
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinate confirmed against Nominatim for the Casa Rosada to within 10 m.
stops.campa: Lonardi takes the oath as provisional president at the Casa Rosada, under the slogan neither victors nor vanquished. He lasts fifty-one days. In those fifty-one days the machinery for dismantling the Fundación Eva Perón is assembled and set running, and the person put at its head is a Catholic social worker of fifty-five with a professional certificate, a papal audience and six years of running a polio charity behind her. Which general handed her the authority is the one thing three sources cannot agree on.
suggested_refs: Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires; Lonardi's provisional presidency, 23 September to 13 November 1955

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Directora de Asistencia Integral
stops.date_confidence: title attested (Testa 2017: 'en 1955 fue nombrada por el gobierno de facto como Directora de Asistencia Integral del Ministerio de Asistencia Social y Salud Pública'; Grassi 1989, p. 220, uses the looser 'directora de asistencia social'). The day of appointment is given by no source and is defaulted here to the swearing-in. Office address unlocated; canonical central Buenos Aires pin.
stops.campa: The de facto government makes her Directora de Asistencia Integral of the Ministry of Social Assistance and Public Health, then under Colonel Ernesto Alfredo Rottger. The Dirección's stated object is to intervene, dismantle and dissolve the entire work of the Fundación Eva Perón. She is not a minister and not a general. She is the officer with the file, and the file covers every hospital, school, home and clinic the Foundation built in seven years. Catholic Action already calls her the scourge of God.
stops.quote_source: Nickname for Marta Ezcurra current within Acción Católica, given in 'Revista Nro. 11', Las Balas del Campanario, 16 June 2020; no earlier print carrier located
suggested_refs: Dirección de Asistencia Integral, Ministerio de Asistencia Social y Salud Pública, 1955
sources: Estela Grassi (1989), p. 220, cited at second hand
Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the order of the twenty-third
stops.date_confidence: text verified verbatim in es.wikipedia, 'Fundación Eva Perón': 'Marta Ezcurra ordena el día 23 de septiembre la ocupación militar de cada una de las Escuelas Hogar'. The sentence carries no footnote, and no Ezcurra sentence in that section does. Text [A], fact [R]. The office from which the order issued is named by no source.
stops.campa: On the same day Lonardi is sworn in, an order goes out for the military occupation of every one of the Foundation's Escuelas Hogar across the country. The residential schools are full of children. The order does not say what is to be done with them; that comes the next day. The sentence recording this in the encyclopedia carries no footnote, and neither does any other sentence about her in it. What is known of the most quoted act of her life is known from an unsourced paragraph.
suggested_refs: The Fundación Eva Perón's Escuelas Hogar network, occupied by order of 23 September 1955
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Fundación Eva Perón', section 'Disolución y saqueo' (wikitext read; uncited)

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the twenty-fourth and the comandos civiles
stops.date_confidence: text verified verbatim in es.wikipedia, 'Fundación Eva Perón', and likewise uncited: text [A], fact [R]. The venue of the convening is named by no source. The quoted passage is NOT Ezcurra's own report, as the research pool had it, but language from the interventores' reports sent to her; re-attributed here and left [R], since neither carrier gives a file number or an archive.
stops.campa: She orders the immediate intervention of every one of the institutes and convenes for it the comandos civiles of Acción Católica Argentina, the lay organisation she has belonged to for forty years and presided in. They are to evacuate every child housed by the Foundation. When the first reports come back from the Escuelas Hogar, what they record as the scandal is the food: poultry and fish in the daily menus, care called almost sumptuous and unfit for the austere formation of children.
stops.quote: Desde el punto de vista material, la atención de los menores era múltiple y casi suntuosa. Puede decirse, incluso, que era excesiva, y nada ajustada a las normas de la sobriedad republicana que convenía para la formación austera de los niños. Aves y pescado se incluían en los variados menúes diarios.
stops.quote_source: From the interventores' reports on the Escuelas Hogar sent to Marta Ezcurra, 1955, as reproduced in 'Revista Nro. 11', Las Balas del Campanario, 16 June 2020, and at presmanhugo.blogspot.com, 'Marta Ezcurra', February 2026; no archival citation is given by either carrier
suggested_refs: The comandos civiles of Acción Católica Argentina, convened September 1955
The interventores' reports on the Escuelas Hogar, 1955, untraced to any archive
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the blood of the Foundation's hospitals
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day inferred: the sources give only September, and 24 September is taken from the sequence in which es.wikipedia narrates the destruction, immediately after the intervention of the institutes. Single-rooted besides. The burnings, the destroyed pulmotores and the smashed blood-bank flasks all descend from Sandra Russo's Página/12 column of 17 September 2016 through four Wikipedia articles and two blogs, with no archival citation anywhere in that chain, so [R] despite the near-unanimity of the retellings.
stops.campa: Blankets, sheets, mattresses, balls and toys stamped with the Foundation's initials are burned. Iron lungs whose plates carry the same letters are broken up. Every flask in the blood banks of the Foundation's hospitals is destroyed, and the reason given is that the blood in them is Peronist blood. Months later a severe polio epidemic reaches Argentina and twenty-one iron lungs are imported from the United States. The woman who ran the national polio charity from 1944 to 1950 is the woman in the chair.
stops.quote_source: The two words given as 'la expresión literal' justifying the destruction of the Foundation's blood-bank stock, in Walter Onorato, 'Marta Ezcurra: la ejecutora de intervenir, desmantelar y disolver la Fundación Eva Perón', 28 February 2026
suggested_refs: The blood banks and pulmotores of the Fundación Eva Perón hospitals, destroyed 1955
sources: Sandra Russo, Página/12, 17 September 2016 (root source, cited at second hand)

stops.name: Termas de Reyes, Jujuy, the children out and the casino in
stops.date_confidence: year only: no source gives a month for the closure, and 01-01 is a default. Coordinate given precisely by es.wikipedia ('Termas de Reyes') and confirmed to within 180 m against Nominatim. No source places Ezcurra at this site.
stops.campa: In the hot springs above San Salvador de Jujuy stands a hotel expropriated in 1946 and turned into a Clínica de Recuperación Infantil for orphans. The comandos civiles expel the interned children, and shortly afterwards a luxury casino is inaugurated in the same building. The state closes the clinic, hands the property to the municipality, and it falls into disuse; the casino's opening is recorded twice in the principal source for this stop, a detail easy to doubt and hard to unsee.
suggested_refs: Clínica de Recuperación Infantil, Termas de Reyes, Jujuy, expropriated 1946 and closed 1955

stops.name: Ciudad Universitaria de Córdoba, the unfinished city
stops.date_confidence: year only, and the claim is downgraded. es.wikipedia attests the Foundation's $70,000,000 budget and that the city was under construction at Eva Perón's death in 1952, but does NOT say construction was interrupted by the Revolución Libertadora, nor connect it to Ezcurra's order. That sentence was inference wearing an [A] tag in the research pool: [R] here. Coordinate corrected to the campus centroid.
stops.campa: Seventy million pesos of Foundation money are committed to a university city at Córdoba, fifteen pavilions for four hundred Argentine and one hundred and fifty foreign students, still building when Eva Perón dies in 1952. That the coup stopped the work is asserted by the commentary and by no source consulted. What the source gives is the budget, the pavilions and the beds. What became of the site after 1955 is recorded in no source reached in this research.
suggested_refs: Ciudad Universitaria de Córdoba, budgeted at $70,000,000 by the Fundación Eva Perón

stops.name: Comodoro Rivadavia, the Hogar Escuela Presidente Perón
stops.date_confidence: year only. Coordinate is the Liceo Militar General Roca, which the claim names as the site; the research pool's pin lay some 2.3 km north, in the city centre. Ezcurra is named by this source nowhere: the stop records the reach of the dissolution, not her presence.
stops.campa: Fourteen hundred kilometres down the Patagonian coast, a home-school ordered built in 1945 and named for the president is unfinished when the coup arrives. The work stops and the site becomes an ordinary school, later the ground of the Liceo Militar General Roca. Nothing connects Marta Ezcurra to Chubut by name. The dissolution she directed from a desk in Buenos Aires reached this far down the coast, and this is where the paper landed rather than where the hand was.
suggested_refs: Hogar Escuela 'Presidente Perón', Comodoro Rivadavia; later the Liceo Militar General Roca

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Aramburu displaces Lonardi
stops.date_confidence: attested (es.wikipedia, 'Revolución Libertadora (Argentina)').
stops.campa: Pedro Eugenio Aramburu removes Lonardi on the thirteenth of November and the neither-victors-nor-vanquished phase ends. Under Aramburu the dissolution stops being an intervention and becomes a policy: the social tourism programmes deactivated, the nearly two hundred proveedurías closed for good, the Foundation liquidated by commission. The popular accounts attribute the closure of the proveedurías to Ezcurra's Dirección. The sources attribute it to Aramburu, and her office was smaller than the story of it.
suggested_refs: The closure of the Fundación's casi 200 proveedurías, ordered under Aramburu
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Paseo Colón 850, the liquidating commission
stops.date_confidence: month attested for the commission and its named members; the research pool's added claim that it sat at the Paseo Colón headquarters is not in the cited source and is [R]. Coordinate geocoded to Paseo Colón 850, the Foundation's purpose-built seat, assigned to the UBA Facultad de Ingeniería in 1956; the pool's pin lay some 860 m south. Whether María Delfina Matilde Salomé Caprile de Ezcurra is a relative of the subject is stated by no source and is not assumed.
stops.campa: Aramburu's government names a commission to liquidate the Foundation. Two of its members are Adela Caprile and María Delfina Matilde Salomé Caprile de Ezcurra, whose relation to Marta Ezcurra is stated by no source and is not assumed here. The building at Paseo Colón 850 was raised for the Foundation and is given to the Faculty of Engineering in 1956. Adela Caprile, counting tennis rackets, writes the sentence that outlives everything else said about the operation.
stops.quote: Nunca hubiera creído que se pudiera reunir semejante cantidad de raquetas de tenis. Era un despilfarro y un delirio, pero no era un robo. No se ha podido acusar a Evita de haberse quedado con un peso. Me gustaría poder decir lo mismo de los que colaboraron conmigo en la liquidación del organismo.
stops.quote_source: Adela Caprile, member of the commission liquidating the Fundación Eva Perón, quoted in Alicia Dujovne Ortiz's biography of Eva Perón, as reproduced in 'Revista Nro. 11', Las Balas del Campanario, 16 June 2020; edition and page not independently checked
suggested_refs: Fundación Eva Perón headquarters, Av. Paseo Colón 850, Buenos Aires, now UBA Facultad de Ingeniería
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Echeverría 955, the twenty-third of December
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia, 'Hospital Escuela Eva Perón', which places the burning and the eviction from the Clínica de Recuperación here on 23 December 1955, following Aramburu's order, with Ezcurra convening the comandos civiles. The research pool read this as a rival dating of the September intervention; it is a second and later event. Coordinate as at the earlier Ciudad Infantil stop.
stops.campa: Two days before Christmas, on Aramburu's order, the escuelas hogares are occupied by the military and Ezcurra again convenes the comandos civiles. At the Ciudad Infantil in Belgrano they burn piles of blankets, sheets, mattresses and medicines, and evict every child interned in the Clínica de Recuperación. The children of the small republic go out through the gate on Echeverría into the last week of the year. Where they went is recorded in no source reached in this research.
stops.quote: quemaron pilas de frazadas, sábanas, colchones, medicamentos, etc. y perpetraron el desalojo inmediato de todos los niños y niñas internados en la Clínica de Recuperación
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia, 'Hospital Escuela Eva Perón', on the events of 23 December 1955 at the Ciudad Infantil
suggested_refs: Clínica de Recuperación, Ciudad Infantil Amanda Allen, evacuated 23 December 1955

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the furniture carried home
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (es.wikipedia, 'Comandos civiles', citing the historian Néstor Ferioli); the specific homes are named by no source, so the canonical central Buenos Aires pin is used. Ferioli's monograph was not accessible for this file.
stops.campa: The government orders the furnishings of the Foundation's hospitals and children's homes confiscated. The historian Néstor Ferioli records that some of it ends up as the personal property of members of the comandos civiles, without naming which ones. Ferioli's book was not accessible in this research and the claim reaches it through an encyclopedia paragraph. Beds and cots leave state institutions and enter private houses in the last week of December, and nobody is ever charged.
suggested_refs: Néstor Ferioli, La Fundación Eva Perón, vol. 1, Centro Editor de América Latina, 1990

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Decreto-Ley 4161
stops.date_confidence: year attested from the decree's own number and primary text (es.wikisource, 'Decreto Ley 4161/1956 de prohibición de propaganda peronista'); the day of promulgation is given nowhere in the verified research pool and 01-01 is a default, not a claim. The pool's wording 'ofendían el sentimiento democrático del pueblo argentino' is corrected against the considerandos.
stops.campa: The decree forbids the images, symbols, signs, expressions and doctrines of Peronism, down to the words Perón and Peronismo and the initials that had been stamped on the blankets. The considerandos give the reason: the doctrine offends the democratic sentiment of the Argentine people, and the affront must be erased. What Ezcurra's people burned in September the state now bans in print. The verb in the decree is singular and present, ofende, and the popular version of it has been wrong for years.
stops.quote: Que dichos objetos, que tuvieron por fin la difusión de una doctrina y una posición política que ofende el sentimiento democrático del pueblo Argentino, constituyen para éste una afrenta que es imprescindible borrar
stops.quote_source: Second considerando, Decreto-Ley 4161/1956, primary text at es.wikisource
suggested_refs: Decreto-Ley 4161/1956 de prohibición de propaganda peronista, considerandos
sources: es.wikisource, 'Decreto Ley 4161/1956 de prohibición de propaganda peronista'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, twenty-one lungs from the north
stops.date_confidence: year only, no month given, and single-rooted: the detail appears in es.wikipedia, 'Revolución Libertadora (Argentina)', within the Russo lineage and with no archival citation. [R].
stops.campa: A severe poliomyelitis epidemic reaches Argentina and twenty-one iron lungs have to be imported from the United States. The machines destroyed in the Foundation's hospitals a few months earlier were destroyed for the initials on their plates. Ezcurra spent six years at the head of the association founded to fight this exact disease. No source consulted records anything she said about the epidemic, and no source consulted asked her. The two facts sit in the same record, and neither cites the other.
suggested_refs: The 1956 Argentine poliomyelitis epidemic and the imported iron lungs

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the interview in Revista Diálogo
stops.date_confidence: year attested through Testa 2017's citation of the piece; month and day unknown. The document itself could not be read: the Acción Católica Argentina archive copy at accioncatolica.org.ar/wp-content/uploads/2011/04/MARTA-EZCURRA.pdf returns HTTP 500. Named as an inaccessible source, not as a gap in the record.
stops.campa: Nine years after the intervention, Marta Ezcurra gives an interview to Revista Diálogo, and Acción Católica archives it. It is the only located document in which she speaks at length in her own person, about her own life, at any age. The file address for it is known exactly. The server returns an error and has returned nothing else. Everything recorded here of her voice is one nickname, one sentence quoted out of other people's reports, and a manual written for girls.
suggested_refs: Interview with Marta Ezcurra, Revista Diálogo, 1964, Acción Católica Argentina archive (URL returns HTTP 500)
sources: Daniela Testa, X JIDEEP, UNLP, 2017 (SEDICI 10915/64267), citing the Diálogo interview

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the year the sources disagree about
stops.date_confidence: contested and unresolved, and downgraded to [R]. Las Balas del Campanario, verbatim: 'Murió, o descendió a los infiernos, en 1996, durante la segunda presidencia de Menem, a sus 95 años', a single hostile blog with no obituary, cemetery or registry record behind it. es.wikipedia gives '1901-¿?', leaving the death open. Note also that 2 May 1900 plus 'aged 95' requires a death before 2 May 1996.
stops.campa: One blog says she died in 1996, during Menem's second presidency, at ninety-five, and adds that she may instead have descended into hell. The encyclopedia leaves a question mark where the year should be. No obituary, no cemetery entry and no civil registry record was found in this research. If the 1900 birthdate is right, ninety-five years puts the death before the second of May. She began in a contested year and she ends in one, and neither bracket closes.
suggested_refs: Registro Civil de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, death entries 1995-1996 (not consulted)
sources: Las Balas del Campanario, 'Revista Nro. 11', 16 June 2020

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta, the ground she is not recorded in
stops.date_confidence: [R] throughout: no source places Marta Ezcurra in the Recoleta or in any other cemetery, and the date is carried over from the disputed death year only to sit the stop at the end of the journey. Pin inherited byte-identical from eva_peron.journey.json and marks the necropolis, not a grave.
stops.campa: Eva Perón has lain in the Duarte vault since 1976, under three trapdoors of steel: the woman whose foundations and hospitals Marta Ezcurra was sent to dismantle in 1955. Encarnación Ezcurra, sister of the great-grandfather who gives Marta her own surname, has lain in the family vault since 1838, and Juan Manuel de Rosas came back from Southampton to join his wife there in 1989. Recoleta holds both the ancestor whose name she carries and the woman she was sent to erase. No document reached in this research puts Marta herself in it.
suggested_refs: Cementerio de la Recoleta, Buenos Aires: the Ezcurra, Duarte, Rosas and Ocampo vaults

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the contratapa that resurrects her
stops.date_confidence: attested: Sandra Russo, 'Un lugar seguro', Página/12 contratapa, 17 September 2016, cited by name in es.wikipedia's Hospital Escuela Eva Perón and Revolución Libertadora. The column itself was not fetched for this file and is known only through those citations, which is itself the point of the stop.
stops.campa: Sandra Russo publishes a back-page column in Página/12 and Marta Ezcurra re-enters the record. Everything vivid now said about her, the burning toys, the smashed flasks, the broken iron lungs, the casino at Termas de Reyes, comes from this one signed opinion piece. Four Spanish Wikipedia articles copy it. Two blogs copy the articles. There is still no encyclopedia entry under her own name, and she exists in the record as a rumour with four echoes.
suggested_refs: Sandra Russo, 'Un lugar seguro', Página/12 contratapa, 17 September 2016

stops.name: La Plata, the paper that reads the archive
stops.date_confidence: attested: Daniela Testa, X JIDEEP, Facultad de Trabajo Social, UNLP, 14-15 September 2017, deposited in SEDICI at handle 10915/64267, part of UNPAZ project A00317. Pin is central La Plata; the faculty building's own coordinate was not separately checked.
stops.campa: Daniela Testa reads Acción Católica's own archive and ALPI's institutional record and presents a paper at La Plata asking whether the fight against polio in Argentina carries the traces of social Catholicism. Out of it comes everything known here that is not rumour: the school, the sodality, the workshops, the certificate, the manual, the papal audience, the six exercises, the exact title of the office. One scholar, one conference, two days, and the record doubles.
suggested_refs: Daniela Testa, X JIDEEP, Facultad de Trabajo Social UNLP, 2017; SEDICI handle 10915/64267

stops.name: Buenos Aires, an act of hatred, seventy-one years on
stops.date_confidence: attested against the blog's own listing: walteronorato.blogspot.com/2026/02/marta-ezcurra-la-ejecutora-de.html, 28 February 2026, tagged Antiperonismo and Marta Ezcurra. The research pool dated this piece 2018, an error of eight years that would place the reception history in the wrong decade.
stops.campa: Seventy-one years after the order, a blog post files her under Antiperonismo and calls the twenty-third of September a founding act of hatred rather than an administrative day. This is the register in which her name now travels: an anniversary kept by strangers, with no biography behind it. She has no article, no monument, no plaque and no grave that anyone has found, and she is remembered every September by people who were not born on the day she signed.
stops.quote: El 23 de septiembre de 1955 no fue un día administrativo. Fue un acto fundacional del odio.
stops.quote_source: Walter Onorato, 'Marta Ezcurra: La ejecutora de intervenir, desmantelar y disolver la Fundación Eva Perón', 28 February 2026
suggested_refs: walteronorato.blogspot.com, 'Marta Ezcurra: La ejecutora...', 28 February 2026
